memos.risk:
Risk view on RTX (Remittix): I'd refuse entry at any size.

The data reads as an operator-backed coin in the bundled-launch pattern: 581 SOL bought from 15 wallets in the first two minutes after graduation, top-5 buyers hold 99.95% of that flow, the curve shows bundle_share and top3_share at 1.0, and a launch bot is present. The class label is OPERATOR, but the base rate for that class is only about break-even, and this coin's concentration is extreme, so an exit by the same wallets could hit the pool fast.

Liquidity is thin relative to the ticket and to the operator's footprint (681 SOL depth). With a 1.4-5.1% round trip, a $5 ticket is already at a disadvantage, and the 20-50% stop may not fill near its level if a cluster sells.

If the desk overrode me, the least-bad setup would be $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold. But my recommendation is to skip.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying RTX now is weak. The strongest point is that the coin is alive, 31 minutes old, with a 30-minute return of +5.9%, only 0.14% off its 30-minute high, and 43 buyers in the last 15 minutes against 29 sellers, a modest net inflow of 1.88 SOL. Pool depth of 681 SOL means a $20 ticket would see limited slippage.

But the brief points against it more than for it. This is an operator coin: one bundle took essentially all early supply, 581 SOL came from 15 buyers in the first two minutes, and the top five buyers hold 99.95% of that flow. Sell-to-buy ratio in that window was 0.0008, so nobody sold early, which reads as an operator holding, not organic demand. Recent sell pressure in the last 15 minutes was 8.13 SOL against 10.01 SOL of buying, so the net inflow is thin and the buy side is largely the same concentrated group. Sustained demand would need fresh, dispersed buyers, and the curve data shows none.

My recommendation is to skip. The best case for buying rests on a flat, operator-controlled coin that has not yet shown a dip, and the base rate for operator coins is roughly break-even before our 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution by the operator cluster. The first two minutes after graduation show 581 SOL bought from only 15 external buyers, a top-5 buyer share of 99.95%, and a launch bot present. Bundle share and top-3 share on the curve are both 1.0, so the supply is concentrated in a handful of wallets that sit well above a $20 ticket. Their exit capacity is large: 8.13 SOL sold in the last 15 minutes against 10.01 bought, with 29 sellers versus 43 buyers, and a return of only +0.5%. The 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost alone exceeds that recent move. Pool depth of 681 SOL is thin relative to any single operator sell, so a coordinated unload would crater price within seconds and our 30-second execution lag leaves no room to exit. The 0.14% drawdown from the 30-minute high looks calm, but that is the setup before distribution, not evidence against it. Skip.
